conversation.content:
Hi there—thank you so much for making time today. My name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician who works with new moms. I’m here to do a quick check-in called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS, to see how you’re feeling emotionally since your baby arrived. It’s simply ten questions about the past seven days, and it helps us spot anything from normal “baby blues” to something more like depression or anxiety so we can get you the right support. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone is in danger. We’ll take it at your pace, and there’s never any judgment—only care. Ready to start?

Question 1: In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt hard to do?
Honestly, it’s been hard. I can still laugh if something’s genuinely funny—like when my sister sent that silly meme—but it feels muted, like I’m forcing it. Nothing really lands the way it used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not very often… I can manage a little chuckle here and there, but most of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I put “only occasionally.” I still get a tiny spark when I think about grabbing coffee with my best friend or maybe taking the baby for a walk if the weather’s nice, but it’s nothing like the excitement I used to feel. Most plans just feel like chores I have to get through.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes… more than I’d like to admit. If the baby won’t settle or I can’t get her to latch right away, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong or I’m just not a good mom. Even little things—like forgetting a burp cloth—turn into, “Ugh, what’s wrong with me?” It’s not every second of the day, but it pops up several times.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah… it’s like there’s a low hum of worry running in the background most of the day. I’ll be folding laundry and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure the baby’s blanket is too loose in the bassinet, even though I just checked her. A few nights this week I’ve lain awake replaying tiny things—like whether I sterilized the bottles right—over and over. Nothing huge happened, but my mind won’t settle.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A couple of times. It’s like a sudden wave—my chest gets tight, I feel shaky, and I have to remind myself to breathe. Once I was just rocking the baby in the nursery and out of nowhere I thought, “What if I drop her?” My heart was racing, but I knew there wasn’t any real danger. It passed after a few minutes, but it left me feeling on edge the rest of the evening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days it feels like I’m barely treading water. I’ll finally get the baby down, see the pile of laundry and dishes, and just want to crawl back into bed. Sometimes I manage to push through, but a couple of times this week I sat on the floor and cried because everything felt like too much. I haven’t used anything to cope—no wine, no pills—but the urge to shut down is definitely there.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I’ll lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning with “what-ifs” about the baby, and I can’t drift off. I’d say three or four nights this week I was still awake more than an hour after I went to bed, and I wake up at least once or twice panicking that I didn’t hear her cry—then I can’t get back to sleep even after I check on her.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty often. I’d say most days this week I’ve felt low or weepy at some point. It’s not every single hour, but it’s like a gray cloud that keeps rolling back in—especially when the house is quiet and I’m alone with the baby.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, once or twice. A couple of evenings ago everything just piled up—I hadn’t showered, the baby wouldn’t nap, my phone was full of “enjoy every moment” posts—and I sat on the couch and cried for maybe ten minutes. It felt like a release, but then the guilt hit for not holding it together better.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

…yes. It’s only flashed through my mind once or twice this week—like a quick, scary “what if I just weren’t here?” kind of thought. I’ve never made any plan and I don’t want to act on it, but the idea did pop in, especially on the really rough nights when I feel like I’m failing her.

You've shared how the past week has felt heavy-laughter comes rarely and feels forced, enjoyment is only a faint spark, and most plans seem like chores. You're blaming yourself for every hiccup with your baby, feel a constant knot of worry, and have had sudden waves of panic. Most days you're overwhelmed to the point of tears, sleep is elusive, and a gray cloud of sadness keeps rolling in. Most importantly, you've had brief, frightening thoughts of not wanting to be here, though you have no plan or intent.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 21, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient reports only occasional, muted laughter, indicating a noticeable reduction in ability to enjoy humor, aligning with "Definitely not so much now"</sym>, <sym>Patient still experiences rare, muted enjoyment ("tiny spark...only occasionally") but overall anticipates plans as burdensome chores, aligning with "Definitely less than I used to."</sym>, <sym>Patient acknowledges frequent self-blame that occurs "several times" a day, aligning with "Yes, some of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes pervasive background anxiety, intrusive racing thoughts, and repetitive worry about routine infant care multiple times per day, aligning with "Yes, very often".</sym>, <sym>Fallback score from text</sym>, <sym>Patient describes feeling overwhelmed "most days," crying on the floor, and strong urges to shut down—matching "most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all."</sym>, <sym>Patient reports sleep disruption most nights this week due to persistent anxious thoughts and panic awakenings, matching "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>"Pretty often... most days this week" aligns with "Yes, quite often," indicating frequent sadness.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** EPDS guidelines classify ≥14 or any positive response on Q10 as high risk; your score of 21 plus endorsement of fleeting self-harm thoughts places you in the urgent-referral category. You describe five or more depressive symptoms present most days for the past seven days: low mood, markedly diminished interest, self-blame, fatigue/loss of energy, sleep disturbance, and recurrent tearfulness, matching DSM-5 criteria for <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. <sym>Anxiety</sym> and <sym>panic</sym> symptoms are also prominent. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Schedule an urgent appointment with your <med>primary care provider</med> or <med>perinatal psychiatrist</med> within the next few days
2. Complete the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale or Patient Safety Screener with a clinician today
3. Arrange practical support-ask a trusted adult to stay with you and help with baby care, meals, and household tasks
4. Begin gentle sleep-hygiene steps: 20-minute wind-down, low lighting, no screens, and consider split-night shifts with a partner
5. Contact a local <med>postpartum support</med> group or 24/7 warmline for peer support and coping ideas
6. Keep this EPDS print-out or screenshot to share with your provider and request a follow-up screen in two weeks
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 21: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale–style interview (10-item)

Symptoms endorsed:
- Persistent low mood, frequent tearfulness  
- Marked loss of enjoyment/interest (anhedonia)  
- Excessive guilt & self-blame re parenting competence  
- Background free-floating anxiety, episodic panic symptoms  
- Sleep initiation/maintenance disturbance (mood-linked)  
- Overwhelm, difficulty coping with daily tasks  
- Transient passive suicidal ideation, no plan or intent reported  

Pattern summary:  
Consistent with moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms with comorbid anxiety features; functional impairment evident (household tasks, sleep, emotional regulation).  

Safety flag:  
Positive endorsement of self-harm ideation ("what if I just weren’t here"), no plan; requires immediate risk assessment and safety planning.

Screening conclusion:  
High clinical concern for postpartum major depressive episode with anxious distress; referral for comprehensive psychiatric evaluation and safety assessment recommended.
